title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: Chicken braised in red wine with lardons and mushrooms
excerpt: Chicken pieces braised in red wine with lardons, chestnut mushrooms, and pearl onions until the wine reduces to a dark, glossy sauce. The great French farmhouse dish, easier than it looks.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coq au vin (literally 'cockerel in wine') is a Burgundian braised chicken dish and one of the best-known examples of French country cooking. Traditionally made with an old rooster (coq), which required long braising to tenderise, the modern version uses a regular chicken or chicken pieces. The dish was popularised in English-speaking kitchens largely by Julia Child, whose recipe in Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961) became the template. The braise develops the wine into a concentrated sauce: use a wine you would drink, as the flavour concentrates considerably.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to hold all the chicken pieces in a single layer.

content.text: Brown the chicken skin-side down in batches and do not rush this step. The colour on the skin creates the base flavour of the final sauce. Pat the pieces completely dry first: wet chicken will not brown, it will steam. The dish takes about 45 minutes in the oven but can also be simmered, covered, on the hob over the lowest heat if that is easier.

Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Pat the chicken dry. Season. Heat the oil in a wide casserole over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken pieces skin-side down in batches for 5 minutes without moving, then turn and cook for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside.

Add the lardons and cook for 4 minutes until golden. Add the whole shallots and cook for 5 minutes, turning, until browned. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and flour. Stir for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and stock. Scrape up any browned bits. Add the thyme and bay leaves.
Return the chicken pieces to the casserole, skin-side up. Bring to a simmer, then transfer to the oven and cook for 45 minutes.

Fry the mushrooms in the butter in a hot frying pan for 5 minutes until golden. Add to the casserole for the last 15 minutes of cooking. Remove the herb sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter with parsley. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.
